- Real behaviour differs from the acceptance text, so the tests assert what the code does. The move response uses `awaiting_signoff` (bool), not `status`. A move with no matching transition returns `transition_not_found`; `move_blocked` appears when a move is re-proposed while a request is pending. The board-list field is `pending_signoff` (a single object), not `pending_signoffs`. The item-level `blocked_reason` is None when some move is open, so blocked reasons are asserted per move in `allowed_moves`; after one sign-off the text reads "awaiting 1 sign-offs" because it counts the remaining sign-offs.
- `signoff_required` can't be triggered over the web path. `SignoffRequiredError` is only mapped in `_work_item_common.py:249` and nothing raises it, so it is not asserted.
- Routes are under `/api/web/...`, not `/teams/...`. Items are seeded with raw SQL because the web path has no mark endpoint. A sign-off by the owner (the proposer) is accepted without counting or refused with 400; the test allows either. I ran `alembic upgrade head` first because `team_workflows` was missing in the test DB.
- The fixture sets `default_team_id` on the workspace user's identity and deletes its `audit_log` rows at teardown, so conftest can delete the identity.
